title: Simple faint at a crowded concert
setting: Hot crowded indoor concert. 19F fainted, collapsed for about 10 seconds. Now alert and responsive, fanned by friends, feeling slightly dizzy.
verdictExplanation: Alert, fully responsive, stable observations. A simple vasovagal faint (syncope) with immediate and complete recovery upon lying flat. Not sick: manage on scene.

shared.circulation: No bleeding, skin color returning to normal (was pale)

history.history: Felt hot, dizzy, and fainted while standing in the crowd. Woke up immediately when she hit the floor.
history.injuries: No injuries from the fall (friends caught her)
history.additional: Had not eaten or drank much water all day

followUp.question: Which of the following would be considered a 'red flag' that indicates this was NOT a simple faint and requires urgent escalation?

options.text: The patient feels embarrassed and wants to leave immediately
The patient remained unresponsive for 5 minutes after falling
The patient was sweating and feeling hot right before collapsing
The patient woke up quickly and feels perfectly fine now

followUp.explanation: A simple vasovagal faint typically results in rapid recovery upon lying flat (within seconds). Remaining unresponsive for several minutes is a major red flag indicating a more serious neurological, cardiac, or metabolic event requiring a 999 call and potential CPR assessment.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Reassure, elevate legs, and give water once fully conscious. Advise her to sit down for a while before walking.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ensure BGL is normal to rule out hypoglycaemia. Check for injuries. Discharge with advice (hydration, rest) if completely recovered and mobile; instruct to seek medical advice if faints recur.
